It was held concurrently with [[2022 United States Senate elections|U.S. Senate elections]] in other states, along with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|elections]] to the [[United States House of Representatives]] and various [[United States elections, 2016#State elections|state]] and [[2022 United States elections#Local elections|local elections]] across the country. The [[incumbent]] senator, [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democrat]] [[Patrick Leahy]], announced on November 15, 2021, that he would not seek re-election to a ninth term,{{Cite web |date=November 15, 2021 |title=Democratic Sen. Patrick Leahy of Vermont, the longest-serving member of US Senate, says he won't run for reelection in 2022 |url=https://news.yahoo.com/democratic-sen-patrick-leahy-vermont-150004018.html |access-date=June 15, 2023 |website=news.yahoo.com |agency=Associated Press}} leaving the seat open for the first time since [[1974 United States Senate election in Vermont|1974]], when Leahy was first elected. Primary elections were held on August 9, 2022, with [[Peter Welch]], the incumbent U.S. Representative from the state's [[Vermont's at-large congressional district|at-large congressional district]], winning the Democratic primary, while [[U.S. Army]] veteran Gerald Malloy won the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] primary. In heavily Democratic Vermont, the Democratic nomination is tantamount to election, and on election day, Welch defeated Malloy in a landslide. He won all but one [[List of counties in Vermont|county in the state]], garnering 68.5% of the vote statewide to Malloy's 28.0%. The race was called for Welch shortly after polls closed.{{Cite web |last1=Kang |first1=Hanna |last2=Casado |first2=Laura |date=November 8, 2022 |title=The Senate has its 1st new member |url=https://theweek.com/2022-election/1018237/the-senate-has-its-1st-new-member |access-date=June 15, 2023 |work=[[The Week]] |location=London}} At 75 years old, Welch became the oldest person ever elected to a first term in the Senate, a record previously held by Massachusetts Republican [[Frederick H. Gillett]], elected in [[1924 United States Senate election in Massachusetts|1924]] at age 73.{{cite web |title=First-time senators take their seats as Democrats maintain slim majority |last=Fedor |first=Lauren |date=January 2, 2023 |url=https://www.ft.com/content/9ebf5b9a-0a23-4f52-8028-b1a8fafafb6f |work=[[Financial Times]] |location=London |access-date=June 15, 2023}} He also became only the second Democrat ever elected to the Senate from Vermont, after Leahy. ==Democratic primary== Following Leahy's announcement that he would retire, speculation arose as to which Democrats could run to succeed him; ''[[Newsweek]]'' cited two of the leading possible contenders for the nomination as [[Peter Welch]], who had served as [[U.S. Representative]] for [[Vermont's at-large congressional district]] since 2006, and [[President pro tempore of the Vermont Senate]] [[Becca Balint]].{{cite web|url=https://www.newsweek.com/who-will-run-patrick-leahys-seat-vermonts-longest-serving-senator-retire-1649350|title=Who Will Run for Patrick Leahy's Seat? Vermont's Longest-Serving Senator to Retire|website=Newsweek|last1=Hutzler|first1=Alexandra|date=November 15, 2021|accessdate=August 16, 2022}} Also considering a run was state representative [[Tanya Vyhovsky]].{{cite web|url=https://theintercept.com/2021/11/14/vermont-senate-seat-patrick-leahy/|title=Bernie Sanders Could Snuff Out a Potential Primary Contest to Replace Patrick Leahy|website=The Intercept|last1=Grim|first1=Ryan|author-link=Ryan Grim|date=November 14, 2021|accessdate=August 16, 2022}} However, candidates were reluctant to enter the race due to speculation that [[Bernie Sanders]], Vermont's popular junior senator, would endorse Welch for the open seat. It was widely considered that an endorsement from Sanders would essentially lock up the race for Welch. While both men were both considered to be associated with the left wing of the Democratic Party, Welch was noted by ''[[The Intercept]]'' to be rather more moderate than Sanders was, especially when compared to Vyhovsky. Welch announced his campaign for the seat on November 22, 2021, pledging in a campaign video to support [[Medicare for All]] and the [[Green New Deal]]; he was immediately endorsed by Sanders.{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2021/11/22/peter-welch-senate-campaign-patrick-leahy-seat-523176|title=Rep.
